sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same experiment: a C-terminal HA tag appended to full-length human OPN1MW (a close paralog of OPN1MW3) expressed via AAV5 in mouse cone photoreceptors. The tag was shown to traffic correctly to cone outer segments and to rescue M-cone ERG function at levels comparable to untagged vector. However, the authoritative topology landmarks place the OPN1MW3 C-terminus (residues 326–364) entirely in the intracellular compartment. A C-terminal tag on a 7-TM opsin sits on the cytoplasmic face, not the extracellular face. No ledger line describes any insertion at an extracellular N-terminus, extracellular loop, or any other surface-exposed position of OPN1MW, OPN1MW3, or any close ortholog. The extracellular N-terminus (residues 1–54) and the four extracellular loops (ECL1: 113–126, ECL2: 192–219, ECL3: 290–304) are topologically accessible but are not grounded by any ledger line. Zero extracellular tag sites are reported.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag appended to full-length OPN1MW (close paralog); validated for correct cone outer-segment trafficking (L2) and functional ERG rescue (L3), but the C-terminus of OPN1MW3 is intracellular (topology landmarks 326–364), so this is not an extracellular surface site.
